transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see us today?

I'm visiting today because I've been struggling a lot with focusing and finishing my tasks. I find it really hard to follow through on instructions, so I often end up leaving my schoolwork and chores half-done. It's just getting really difficult to manage lately.
Do you also experience symptoms like restlessness, fidgeting, or feeling constantly 'on the go' that makes it hard for you to sit still or engage in quiet activities?
No, I don't really experience those kinds of symptoms. I don't usually feel physically restless or have trouble sitting still, so that's not really an issue for me.
How long have you been experiencing these difficulties with focus and task completion, and did they start when you were a child or did they develop more recently?
These difficulties have been really severe for about two years and three months now. But looking back, I actually first started struggling with these things as a child, definitely before I turned 12.
Can you tell me more about how these difficulties with focus and task completion are affecting your daily life, such as your relationships, work, or school performance?

It's causing a lot of disruption because I struggle to finish tasks at school, work, or even simple chores at home. I also constantly forget daily responsibilities like paying bills on time, keeping appointments, and returning calls. It's incredibly frustrating because I feel like I'm constantly falling behind in my daily life.
Do you use any specific strategies or tools, such as planners, reminders, or apps, to help you stay organized and manage your time more effectively?

I don't really use any specific tools right now. I've tried using planners and setting phone reminders in the past, but I always end up forgetting to check them. They just don't seem to work for me because I can't even remember to use them.
Do you find that you have difficulty remembering instructions or conversations, or do you often lose your train of thought in the middle of tasks or conversations?

Yes, I definitely have a hard time remembering instructions, which is why I struggle to follow through and finish my chores or work tasks. I'm also generally very forgetful in my daily life. I'm not really sure about losing my train of thought in conversations, though.
Can you describe a typical situation where you start a task, and how you usually feel or what happens as you try to continue working on it over a period of time, say 30 minutes to an hour?

If I sit down to write a report, I start with the best intentions of following the guidelines and getting it done. However, after about 15 minutes, my mind drifts, I completely lose track of the instructions, and I walk away to do something else. By the end of the hour, the task is left completely unfinished.
On a scale of 1 to 10, with 1 being minimal impact and 10 being severe impact, how would you rate the severity of your symptoms and their effect on your daily life?

I'm not really sure of an exact number, as I haven't really thought about my struggles in terms of a scale. But I can say that it has been incredibly challenging and frustrating to deal with lately. It definitely has a major impact on my ability to get through my daily life.
Would you say that your symptoms are having a significant enough impact on your daily life that you would consider them to be around an 8, 9, or even a 10 out of 10 in terms of severity?

I'm still not sure how to rate it on a scale of 1 to 10, as I haven't really thought about it in those exact numbers. But I can say that my constant difficulties with forgetting things and finishing tasks do cause a lot of frustration in my daily life.
Can you think of any recent situations where your symptoms significantly interfered with an important task or event, and how did you manage to cope with the challenges you faced?

Just last week, I completely missed an important dental appointment because I forgot all about it, and I also failed to finish a major report at work because I couldn't follow through on the instructions. I tried to cope by putting sticky notes all over my desk and setting phone alarms, but I still ended up overlooking them. It was incredibly frustrating and stressful to deal with.
